claim: Emoji are stripped and standalone four-digit years are read as years; plain integers and decimals are left to eSpeak, which already renders them as words.

listen_check.instructions: Play before.wav then after.wav. Two audible differences: the before side speaks the emoji name aloud, and reads 1999 as 'one thousand nine hundred ninety-nine' where the after side says 'nineteen ninety-nine'.

isolation_probe.method: each transform isolated: same sentence synthesized pre-change vs post-change, durations in seconds

integer_42.verdict: no-op — eSpeak already expands plain integers

decimal_314.verdict: no-op — eSpeak already expands simple decimals

year_1999.verdict: KEPT — cardinal reading became a year reading

emoji_tada.verdict: KEPT — Kokoro was speaking the emoji name aloud

isolation_probe.conclusion: The task's premise was half wrong. Kokoro/eSpeak ALREADY renders plain integers and simple decimals as words, so that half of the requirement was satisfied before this change. General number expansion was implemented, measured as a no-op, found to garble adjacent forms (555-1234, 2026-08-11, $5, R2D2, 12:00), and REMOVED. What shipped is only what measured a difference: emoji stripping and standalone four-digit year reading.

scope_decision: D008 — general number expansion removed after measurement; see 002_PLAN/decisions/
